## Symptom

Every `tauri-agent-tools` verb that needs the page (`eval`, `dom`, `click`,
`rust-logs` via the CLI) **times out**, while `probe` shows the bridge process
and its port, and `curl http://127.0.0.1:<bridge-port>/version` answers 200.
Multiple agents independently diagnosed this as "the Tauri shell is wedged"
and killed/relaunched shells for hours (2026-07-03: pids 763783, 55852 — the
fresh relaunch "wedged" identically). WebKit CPU near 100% reinforced the
misread; it was just a heavy live page.

## Root cause

The bridge's injected eval JS returns its result to Rust via
`invoke("__dev_bridge_result")`. Tauri 2's ACL only allows an app command from
the SPA's **remote http origin** (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` — which is how the
operator SPA always loads) when:

1. the command is listed in `build.rs` →
   `tauri_build::AppManifest::new().commands(&[...])`, which autogenerates an
   `allow-<command>` permission, **and**
2. that permission is granted in `capabilities/default.json` (whose
   `remote.urls` covers `http://127.0.0.1:*`).

Commands registered only through tauri-specta's `collect_commands!` get **no
autogenerated permission** — the build scans `generate_handler!`, not specta.
`__dev_bridge_result` was in the specta list only, so the invoke was rejected
(`__dev_bridge_result not allowed`, visible **only** in the web inspector as
an unhandled promise rejection), the eval ran but could never reply, and the
CLI timed out. This is the same class WI-1976 fixed for the native-shell
commands (`console_launch` etc.) — the KEEP-IN-SYNC comment in `build.rs` is
the contract.

## Diagnosis recipe (60 seconds, no guessing)

- Bridge answers `/version` but evals time out → **suspect ACL, not a hang**.
- Screenshot the window (`DISPLAY=:N import -window root out.png` on a
  headless instance) and look at the web-inspector console for
  `Command … not allowed` rejections.
- Do **not** kill/relaunch shells for this symptom — a fresh instance fails
  identically because the block is in the binary's ACL, not process state.

## Fix pattern (any new webview-invoked app command)

Two edits, then rebuild: add the command name to `AppManifest.commands` in
`build.rs`, and add the generated identifier (underscores → hyphens, so
`__dev_bridge_result` → `allow---dev-bridge-result`) to
`capabilities/default.json`. `cargo build` validates the pair. Running shells
need a restart to pick up the new ACL; the `tauri dev` watcher rebuilds and
respawns its app automatically when `src-tauri` changes.
